sections.what: Vecino Health Centers provides medical, dental and counseling services in northeast Houston. Its Denver Harbor family center and Airline children’s and women’s center serve insured and uninsured families in English and Spanish. Income-based fees, public insurance acceptance and multidisciplinary care aim to make continuing treatment accessible.
sections.monitoring: Original FY2024 reports 11,453 medical patients and 29,099 encounters, including children. The 1,070 behavioral clients and 330 dental patients may overlap and are not added. Request unique adult households, clinical completion, measured patient utility, actual incremental payments and partner resources. HRSA quality awards indicate clinical process performance, not causal donation-funded QALYs. Both Houston locations accept Medicaid, CHIP, Medicare and private insurance; alternatives and reimbursement are part of the baseline.
sections.qualitative: Original recipient returns distinguish medical patients from encounters and overlapping service groups. The official donor page and original return agree on the healthcare recipient EIN. Current locations and insurance/sliding-fee arrangements make service access and counterfactuals inspectable. Clinical quality recognition does not establish additional health effects or household savings. Adult household mapping, response, utility and net resources remain unsupported local priors. Public reimbursements, partner clinical resources and a property affiliate complicate marginal funding and full resource scope. Official donor EIN 76-0622208 matches Houston Community Health Centers Inc; facility affiliate 82-5421842 is not the donation healthcare recipient. Denver Harbor is a Houston neighborhood, not Colorado. Recipient-owned giving route is verified, not checkout or marginal capacity.
sections.cost: The conditional annual limited-channel reference is $47.32 million per ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents: 2.673913 clinical QALYs plus -0.335658 signed resource equivalents. $10,000 corresponds to 0.002113 combined equivalents under proportional annual accounting, not verified next-gift response. Whole-parent recognized annual resources are $11,065,389. Observed 11,453 medical patients × judged .6 adult-household mapping × .2 additional annual response yields 1,374.36 household proxies; .6 is not an observed unique adult count or extra clinical success rate. The clinical subset of 274.872 receives judged .02 utility for .5 finite years, not a process award-to-QALY conversion. Independent resource success .2 with hypothetical $200 actual otherwise-paid expenses avoided after alternative providers, taxes and benefits uses positive overlap .5 minus full $30 one-off travel, childcare, foregone-pay or copay burden. Success households net $70; others lose full $30. One welfare-equivalent adult per household, $20,000 annual consumption and one joint log. No retail medications, gross salary or ordinary survivor wages. Clinical failure retains resources and burdens; union harms are full and positive-only overlap never discounts negative resources. ResourceYears means realized fraction of one year’s gain, not perpetual savings. Provider/property opportunity costs are distinct from participant costs; central external zero is unknown-neutral, not observed zero. Whole-parent expense versus narrow adult channel is not complete portfolio or marginal-donation EV.
sections.funding: FY2024 parent tax expense $10,482,273 plus Schedule D excluded donated resources $583,116 = $11,065,389; FY2023 $10,613,110 + $700,118 = $11,313,228; FY2022 $11,696,526 + $702,798 = $12,399,324. This is a consistent parent recognized-expense plus donated-resource basis. FY2022 audit reconciliation also identifies property-affiliate expense $546,553 less intercompany rent $140,548 and asset-disposal loss $4,836; these are not blindly added again. Bad debt $992,399 is in tax expense; it is not recipient household loss or provided-care retail benefit. Affiliate consolidated economic scope and partner opportunity costs remain unknown/stressed. FY2024 program service revenue $6,407,003 underscores insurance reimbursement rather than pure donation-supported access.

model.costScope: Whole annual recipient recognized resources; limited clinical/resource numerator; marginal additional cost unknown
model.geographicAttribution: Both healthcare centers are in Houston; .98 local patient share is an explicit judgment, not measured county distribution.
model.formula: Union=N*unique*b; clinical=union*completion*q*discounted finite years minus full union harms. Financial=.5*people*discounted one-year log(1+joint net gain/baseline), local share once. Headline=10*C/(clinical+financial).
model.counterfactual: Medicaid, CHIP, Medicare, private insurance, other FQHC/charity care, sliding fees and partner-supported treatment remain baseline; only additional annual appropriate care and actual net resources count.
model.attribution: Annual incremental recipient response is distinct from cohort deduplication and geographic share; no claim of whole annual portfolio or marginal donation causal effect.
model.uncertainty: Source-grounded cost and service description; numerical clinical and disposable-resource effects are unsupported conditional hypotheses. Complete total EV remains unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Medical patients, additional appropriate completed care and finite adult symptom relief; encounters and overlapping dental/behavioral groups are not additional people.
